BiblicalUsage: Mishael is one of Daniel's three companions in Babylon, the young man the king's court renames Meshach. In this verse Daniel goes home and tells Mishael, Hananiah and Azariah what the king has demanded, so they can seek mercy from God together before the night is out.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Mishael matters here because he prays with his friends: the wisdom that saves them all comes to men who seek God together, not alone.
RelatedTopics: Faithfulness in exile; Prayer; Friendship with Christ
